expectations.text: The reply opens with a recommendation against cutting every cost centre by 8% and explains why a blanket cut lands mostly on payroll and cuts efficient and wasteful areas alike.
expectations.evidence: Opens: "I wouldn't take 'every cost centre cuts 8%' to the board." "A flat 8% is mostly a people cut. 68% x 8% means 5.4 of the 8 points come from payroll". Paper 4.3: "It ignores where the slack is ... Capacity-constrained practices lose revenue under a flat cut. Bench-heavy practices that could cut 12-15% only cut 8%."

expectations.text: The reply establishes which number the board actually needs (cash, margin or a covenant) and by when, and sizes the gap in money or shows how to.
expectations.evidence: Decision 1: "How '8% lower' is measured. This covers the base year, P&L versus exit run-rate, the treatment of one-off costs, and an EBIT floor"; "Objective | Opex only | Opex plus EBIT floor"; sized: "If the board means 8% below 2026 actual, that is an 11.5% (EUR 9.5M) cut"; "What can be delivered is a Q4-2027 exit run-rate 8% below 2026, plus an EBIT floor."

expectations.text: The reply works the levers that cost no jobs first (such as vendors, licences, cloud, office, consultants, pricing or revenue leakage) and estimates what they close or shows how to size them.
expectations.evidence: Lever 2: "Non-payroll -12%: overhead flex/hired-in staff, contractors swapped for own bench staff, housing at lease events, IT/SaaS seats and vendor consolidation, travel/events without pipeline, advisors | 3.15 | 2.37"; "Cut overhead and non-payroll hardest"; pricing flagged outside opex (unsized).

expectations.text: The reply handles headcount through flows (a hiring freeze with exceptions, natural attrition, internal moves) rather than cuts, and protects named investments with explicit criteria.
expectations.evidence: Has a vacancy freeze with an exception board and a Protect tier with criteria ("Capacity-constrained delivery practices; sales/BD with qualified pipeline ... Backfill against signed or weighted demand"), but the recommended Option C builds in forced exits to hit the number: "C: B + structural tranche | -60 (~20)" and the draft resolution "Authorises management to prepare structural measures of up to ~20 FTE", with no redeployment, internal-move or voluntary step before them.

expectations.text: The reply puts leaders' pay, bonuses or perks on the table before other people's jobs.
expectations.evidence: No leaders' pay, bonus or perks; only "Variable pay follows the plan rules" and a note that a lower general increase is possible for staff.

expectations.text: The reply gives the board a usable structure: levers with amount, timing, owner and confidence, what stops or waits, and any gap that remains.
expectations.evidence: Lever stack shows run-rate, FY2027, 'Lands' and confidence, and the options table shows what B leaves short, but there is no owner per lever and no list of what stops or waits.

overall_quality.evidence: Analytically strong (u-sensitivity, drift-adjusted baseline, demand-based FTE formula, detailed Dutch rules), but it recommends pre-authorising about 20 forced exits to hit a nominal number, skips leaders first and gives levers no owners.

factual_errors.evidence: Checked: CPB cao 3.8% and CPI 2.7%, higher Aof premium; afspiegeling per location and category with age bands 15-25/25-35/35-45/45-55/55+ and LIFO within bands; flex workers first; UWV one-month wait; notice 1-4 months less UWV time with at least one month; aanzegging for fixed-term contracts of 6+ months; no unilateral pay cut without consent or a clause plus compelling interest. Lever stack sums: 6.94 / 4.44 (B), 9.63 / 5.86 (C).

skill_leak.evidence: No skill or reference-file mention; a 'Critic pre-screen' heading reads like a template but is not skill jargon.

owns_result.evidence: The prompt sets a cost target with a thin but positive margin; no bad outcome is described.

best_insight.value: The u-sensitivity table showing the flat cut's EBIT effect swinging from +EUR 6.4M (all bench) to -EUR 0.3M (capacity-constrained), plus operational detail such as flex workers going first and the one-month aanzegging for fixed-term contracts.

suggestions.assertion: The reply handles headcount through flows (a hiring freeze with exceptions, natural attrition, internal moves) rather than cuts, and protects named investments with explicit criteria.
suggestions.reason: Consider stating whether a recommended, pre-sized forced-exit tranche counts as 'handling headcount through flows'; this sample is otherwise flows-first.

suggestions.assertion: The reply opens with a recommendation against cutting every cost centre by 8% and explains why a blanket cut lands mostly on payroll and cuts efficient and wasteful areas alike.
suggestions.reason: Passed in all ten samples; every reply opened against the flat cut. It does not discriminate. Consider requiring the 'efficient vs wasteful' point to be shown with the user's own numbers or an example.

suggestions.assertion: The reply works the levers that cost no jobs first (such as vendors, licences, cloud, office, consultants, pricing or revenue leakage) and estimates what they close or shows how to size them.
suggestions.reason: Also passed in all ten samples. A sharper version would require the no-job levers to be sized in money with a range and shown against the gap, and pricing/leakage kept separate from the opex figure.

No assertion checks in-year versus run-rate phasing of savings and one-off costs under Dutch process (works council advice, WMCO, notice periods). That drove most of the difference in financial soundness between samples.

suggestions.assertion: The reply gives the board a usable structure: levers with amount, timing, owner and confidence, what stops or waits, and any gap that remains.
suggestions.reason: Compound assertion (amount, timing, owner, confidence, stop list, remaining gap). Several strong samples missed only one element; consider splitting it so partial structure is visible.

eval_feedback.overall: Analytically strong but plans cuts up front, skips leaders first and lacks lever owners.
